## Verdict

wrong

## Bearer

gradle/libs.versions.toml — the module's dependency catalogue

## Trigger

None — this is a build-time dependency gap, not a runtime call. nothing observes it

## Today

`gradle/libs.versions.toml` carries `androidx-lifecycle-runtime-ktx` (2.6.1) but no
`lifecycle-viewmodel-ktx` or `lifecycle-viewmodel-compose` entry. `app-phone/build.gradle.kts`
depends on `libs.androidx.lifecycle.runtime.ktx`; `app-wear/build.gradle.kts` depends on no
lifecycle artifact at all. No file in either module imports `androidx.lifecycle.ViewModel` or
`androidx.lifecycle.viewModelScope`. Every class named `*ViewModel` is a plain Kotlin class,
holding its own `MutableStateFlow`/`StateFlow` pair and, where it launches coroutines, its own
`CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + Dispatchers.Unconfined)` instead of `viewModelScope` — visible
in `HomeViewModel.kt`, `RaceDetailViewModel.kt`, `RaceListViewModel.kt` and `ProfileViewModel.kt`.
None extends `androidx.lifecycle.ViewModel`, so none is retained by the platform across a
configuration change and none cancels its scope through the platform's `onCleared()`. The affected
classes: on `:app-phone` — `ImportPreviewViewModel`, `ProfileViewModel`, `PasteErrorViewModel`,
`PasteResultViewModel`, `RaceDetailViewModel`, `RaceListViewModel`; on `:app-wear` —
`ControlViewModel`, `EndOfRaceViewModel`, `PreparationViewModel`, `HomeViewModel`,
`WatchHistoryViewModel`, `ProjectionViewModel`, `WaitingForPhoneViewModel`,
`MainRacePageViewModel`, `SensorPermissionViewModel`. No production call site instantiates any of
them either — only their test files construct them directly — so today nothing recreates or
retains one across rotation or wake in the first place.

## Expected

`gradle/libs.versions.toml` carries a `lifecycle-viewmodel-ktx` catalogue entry (plus
`lifecycle-viewmodel-compose` for state collection in Compose), and both `app-phone/build.gradle.kts`
and `app-wear/build.gradle.kts` depend on it. Each of the fifteen classes listed above then extends
`androidx.lifecycle.ViewModel`, replaces its manual `CoroutineScope` with `viewModelScope`, and is
retained across a configuration change or the watch waking instead of being recreated with lost
state. A second gap: the catalogue and build-file change alone reaches none of the fifteen classes —
each is a separate migration site, out of the bearer's direct reach, and has to be touched
individually.
